# CANON — *The Long Book*

Hard facts, sourced. Granular enough to catch a contradiction introduced in
chapter five. Anything marked **HARD RULE** may not be bent for any scene.

---

## Geography

- The Shelf is the delta and lower valley of the river Nissa; its city is
  Amrith, at the mouth. (world.md)
- Amrith has three parts: the Stone Ait (limestone island, second reach,
  Reckoning House), the Low Wharfs (working city), Kell Ammar (salt-house
  district, eastern edge). (world.md)
- The Low Wharfs flood at every second tide. Doors are on the upper floor.
  (world.md, ch 4)
- The Whiting is forty miles of dead salt flat east of Amrith and is the only
  warranted sink on the Shelf. (world.md)
- Whiting landmarks: the Nine Marks (walkers' cairns), the Shell Bank (a
  two-mile dead-cockle ridge; Yannu's hut), the Wallow (the north lobe).
  (world.md)
- The Whiting has no birds. The crust ticks audibly as it cools. Air dries
  the eye within a minute. (world.md, ch 2)
- The Sarrow is six fen villages between the Third and Fifth Reaches:
  Sarrow-under-Wall, Little Sarrow, Ferrey, Wick, Ounds, and the station at
  Kell Ammar. About 1,900 people. Tenure runs through House Nesuir. (world.md)
- Sarrow-under-Wall is the oldest set-down ground on the Shelf. (ch 29)
- Kethren is the sour upland country, nine days up the Nissa by barge and
  four back down. Worked by hand and lime under the 1104 Concession.
  (world.md)
- Sur Ellun is the outer isles at the Shelf's lip, two days' sail, abandoned
  since 1148. The water there is deep and moving. (world.md)
- **Travel times.** Amrith → Whiting's edge: half a day by punt plus three
  hours on foot. Amrith → the Sarrow: two days upriver. Amrith → Kethren:
  nine days up, four down. Amrith → Sur Ellun: two days' sail. A letter to
  Kethren and its answer is three weeks. (world.md, HARD RULE)
- The calendar has ten months of thirty-six days: Thaw, Green, Highwater,
  Longsun, Dust, Ebb, Whitening, Rime, Deepwinter, Turn. (world.md)
- The year's lowest tides fall in Deepwinter. The largest workings can only
  be done then. (world.md, HARD RULE)

---

## Timeline

- The Whiting was warranted as common sink in 1010. Set-downs elsewhere have
  been forbidden since. (world.md)
- The Reckoning House was founded at Amrith between 1004 and 1041. (world.md)
- The Third Order — the law of composition — was enacted in 1063. The
  acceleration clause has been printed on the face of every composition since.
  (world.md)
- The Kethren Concession (1104) forbids upland farms to hire Shelf pairs.
  (world.md)
- The Sur Ellun trials failed in 1148. Eleven setters died. No set is
  possible into moving water. (world.md, HARD RULE)
- **1200 — the Nesuir Failure.** Ines Ottun founders at the eleventh carry
  drawing blight from the Nesuir seed-granaries at Ferrey. Four thousand
  quarters of seed lost. (world.md)
- **1201 — the Hungry Year.** No planting on the middle Nissa. Assessment
  entered against Ines Ottun and *the drawing line of Ottun*: 2,140 carries.
  Bel Osse, aged 26, writes the mortality return by hand: 4,100 names.
  (world.md, characters.md)
- 1203 — Ines Ottun dies, three years foundered, carrying blight. (characters.md)
- 1210 — Veth Dral, full grey at 28, walks out onto the Whiting. Yannu walked
  him out. (characters.md, ch 34)
- **1211 — the Ottun Composition** contracted. Sahra was nineteen and signed
  it herself. (world.md)
- 1213 — Yannu Dral takes the walker's warrant for the eastern lobes.
  (characters.md)
- 1216 — the Whiting's warranted margin contracts for the first time on
  record. The House files it as *silting*. Turi Osse pensioned, full grey.
  (world.md, characters.md)
- **The book runs 9 Thaw 1219 to 27 Deepwinter 1219 — ten months.**
  (outline.md)
- Ch 1–11 span 9 Thaw to 12 Highwater: 93 days. (outline.md)
- The climax working is on 24 Deepwinter 1219, the lowest tide of the year.
  (outline.md, HARD RULE)

## Magic System Rules

- The trade is called the Draw. It has two halves — drawers and setters —
  and no third. (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- A load is a *quality*, not a substance: salt, rot, fever, blight, souring.
  The thing it came out of is left clean. Nothing is added anywhere.
  (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- Draw and set are congenital. Draw runs about 1 in 400 births on the Shelf;
  set about 1 in 3,000. Neither can be taught, bought, or acquired.
  (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- Between the thing and the ground, a load lives in a body and is felt there.
  (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- **Capacity is measured in carries.** A carry = the salt of one cistern of
  200 barrels, or the rot of one granary bay, or the fever off nine people.
  (world.md)
- Ordinary capacity: 3–4. Strong: 8–9. Sahra Ottun: 14. The Long Book's
  record is 15, and the man who set it foundered proving it. (world.md,
  characters.md)
- **Foundering:** past capacity, the load becomes the drawer's own condition,
  permanently, and capacity does not recover. The one sign is that **the
  thirst stops**. (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- A setter passes and cannot hold. A set requires ground that will take it,
  skin against skin, and time. (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- **Grey:** one span — a fingerbreadth — per two hundred carries passed,
  permanent, from the fingertips inward. Reported as a location on the body.
  (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- **The jump:** more than three carries in one pass and the loss leaves the
  hands and takes a sense or a region, permanently. (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- **A load moves one way only: thing → drawer → setter → ground.** No
  drawer-to-drawer, no setter-to-setter, no relays, no lending, no giving
  back. (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- Only dead ground takes. Living ground takes only by dying, dies widely, and
  gives the load back within a generation. Setting into living ground is
  treated as arson under the Third Order. (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- No set into moving water; no set above the tideline; no set at flood.
  (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- **A carried load can be read** off any body by any drawer — whitened
  cuticles, sweet wrists, wet eyes. This is the only form of observation at a
  distance in this world. There is no scrying, no sending, no familiar, and
  **no bond of any kind between any two people.** (world.md, **HARD RULE**)
- Ground does not end a load. Ground *carries* it, and ground has a capacity.
  The Whiting has been carrying since 1010 and is now foundering. (world.md,
  ch 23)
- **A setter keeps a fraction of every load, permanently, and what he keeps
  is ended.** Grey is not damage; grey is the load, finished. This is the
  only place in the world a load stops. (world.md, ch 36)
- The Draw cannot heal a wound, mend a bone, restore a sense, or lengthen a
  life. It takes conditions only. **Nothing in this book is undone.**
  (world.md, **HARD RULE**)

### Fixed sensations (may not vary by scene)

| Load | Sits in | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| Salt | blood | thirst water does not touch; whitening at hairline and cuticles; coin taste at the back of the throat; skin that squeaks under a thumb |
| Rot | joints | sweetness at the wrists, smellable across a table; give in the knees like wet rope; a slow turning-over sound in the ear |
| Fever | marrow | wet-looking eyes; cold hands, hot breastbone; a hum in the back teeth |
| Blight | nails, hair | ridged nails lifting at the bed; hair going at the temple; cut grass gone over |
| Souring | lungs | a cough with no sickness under it; a taste of standing water |
| Setting | the setter's hands | cold from the inside out, then hot, then nothing; a whine pitched at the jaw |

## Prices Paid

Every entry is permanent. Nothing on this list is returned, healed, or
reversed anywhere in the book.

- Weyl Ammar gave one span of grey in ch 1, and four more across the book.
  He is at four spans a year and will be full grey by forty. (ch 1)
- Yannu Dral lost the smell of smoke in ch 8 — four carries in one pass for a
  fen family who could not pay. (ch 8)
- Sahra Ottun took a permanent whitening at the hairline in ch 9, at
  thirteen of fourteen. Cosmetic, permanent, and readable by any assessor.
  (ch 9)
- Sahra seated half a carry of rot in her left knee during the live pass at
  Sarrow-under-Wall in ch 15. The knee gives for the rest of her life. (ch 15)
- Sahra seated one carry of rot in her right shoulder retaking the returned
  load at the reopened north lobe in ch 27. (ch 27)
- Yannu Dral lost taste entirely in ch 30 — four carries in one pass, to keep
  Sahra off seventeen. (ch 30)
- Sahra seated two carries in ch 30 and has carried a new thirst baseline
  since. (ch 30)
- Turi Osse lost the sight of his left eye in ch 31, taking three carries off
  a child at Sarrow-under-Wall. (ch 31)
- Sarrow-under-Wall: nine dead on 28 Rime, thirty-one by Deepwinter. The
  village is condemned and is not resettled. (ch 31)
- Turi Osse lost sensation from the chest inward in the demonstration in
  ch 39, and died of unfelt cold on the second tide in ch 40. (ch 39, ch 40)
- **Sahra Ottun foundered at the Wallow on 24 Deepwinter 1219.** She carries
  salt permanently, has a thirst that nothing touches, and **has no capacity
  and will never draw again.** (ch 43–44, **irreversible**)
- **Yannu Dral went full grey at the Wallow on 24 Deepwinter 1219** — no
  touch, no smell, and what taste remained. About two thousand carries in one
  continuous pass. (ch 44, **irreversible**)

## Relationship Beats

- Sahra Ottun and Yannu Dral meet on 2 Green 1219, on the mud at Kell Ammar,
  under a standing order. It is the same event that drags her into the
  Whiting's failure. (ch 5)
- She asks what a set will cost him before she asks whether he will do it, on
  11 Green. He stops walking. (ch 7)
- They touch for the first time on 10 Longsun, during the live pass at the
  Sarrow-under-Wall well, and neither remarks on it. (ch 15)
- She tells him about the four hours at twenty-two on 28 Longsun, at the
  Shell Bank. It is the first thing she has told anyone. (ch 18)
- **First deliberate touch: 11 Ebb, ch 23.** Her palm flat against his, in
  the place where he can still feel, for sixteen seconds, counted aloud. She
  uses the word *want* for the first time in the book. (ch 23)
- She tells him she was relieved when she signed at nineteen. It cannot be
  unsaid. (ch 23)
- **The break happens on 4 Deepwinter, ch 33, over the acceleration of the
  composition — not over a secret, a rival, or a misunderstanding.** Nothing
  in that chapter is untrue or unknown to either of them. (ch 33)
- He offers a bond-setter's indenture in ch 33; she refuses to let him; the
  refusal is what neither can forgive. (ch 33)
- She asks him, out loud and in front of witnesses, to be the setter at the
  Wallow, on 23 Deepwinter. (ch 41)
- They choose each other on the page on 26 Deepwinter, both alive, both
  present, in a room with eleven other people in it. (ch 45)

## Character Facts

- Sahra Ottun, 27 (b. 1192). Assessed capacity fourteen. Left thumb carries
  the Nesuir tally-ring, turned inward. (characters.md)
- Sahra has not deliberately touched another person since 1208. (characters.md)
- Sahra foundered once before, at twenty-two, for four hours, and has never
  told the House. If it were known her rating would be struck. (characters.md,
  ch 18)
- Sahra has been drawing off the books for fen families for three years, in
  breach of the composition. (characters.md)
- Sahra keeps a chipped clay cup filled and never finishes it. (ch 1)
- Yannu Dral, 33 (b. 1186), Kethren-born, came to Amrith in 1205.
  (characters.md)
- Yannu's grey at story start: to the wrist on the right hand, to the second
  knuckle on the left. He has lied about the last two spans on two annual
  assessments. (characters.md)
- Yannu has passed about eleven hundred carries in fourteen years.
  (characters.md)
- Yannu tests surfaces with the back of the hand above the second knuckle,
  never the palm. (characters.md)
- Yannu salts everything and never says why. (characters.md)
- Yannu falsified warrants for six years, seriously for two. (characters.md)
- Veth Dral, Yannu's brother, sold a twenty-year bond-setter's indenture at
  nineteen and was full grey at twenty-eight. His boots are on a nail in
  Yannu's hut. (characters.md)
- Dovra Nesuir, 62, matriarch of House Nesuir — the smallest of the three
  great houses and the only one carrying an assessment on its own books. Her
  husband hanged himself at Ferrey in spring 1201. (characters.md)
- Halim Nesuir, 31, found his father's body at twelve. (characters.md)
- Bel Osse, 54, Chief Reckoner since 1214. Turi Osse is her father's younger
  brother; they have been estranged since she certified the pension ordinance
  in 1216. (characters.md)
- Turi Osse, 66, full grey since 1216, pensioned at a third rate, mends nets
  by sight at the Kell Ammar salt-house. (characters.md)
- Sefa Quenn, 58, washer, no capacity of any kind, no entry in the Long Book.
  Mother of under-reckoner Merrow Quen. (characters.md)
- Ansa Rask, 40, fen-reeve of the Sarrow, elected three times; held the
  stock-book through the Hungry Year at twenty-two. (characters.md)
- Yeshin Ottun, 14, Sahra's cousin, manifested at eleven. Named in the
  composition's schedule as the drawing line of Ottun, to be assessed at
  sixteen. (characters.md)

## Political / Factional

- The Reckoning House holds the Long Book, assesses capacity, standardises
  the carry, warrants ground, and enforces obligations denominated in
  carries. It cannot tax, raise troops, or make law. (world.md)
- The House may declare a hazard at any time, and a declared hazard carries a
  **standing order**: compulsory service by any name in the Long Book at one
  third the open rate. (world.md, ch 4, ch 5)
- **A working performed on the House's account and witnessed by a reckoner is
  credited against the worker's entry at the assessed rate.** (world.md, ch 3,
  ch 20, HARD RULE — this is the instrument that discharges the composition
  in ch 44)
- A struck walker is assessed; a walker assessed past the wrist is retired.
  (world.md, ch 4)
- The Chief Reckoner outranks any house. A house outranks a fen-reeve. A
  standing order outranks a private contract. (world.md, HARD RULE)
- The three great houses are Nesuir, Ammar, and Dell. Nesuir is the smallest
  and the most exposed. (world.md)
- House Nesuir has pledged the Ottun composition forward as security against
  its own obligations to the Reckoning House. (world.md, ch 10)
- The Sarrow's tenure runs through the Nesuir estate. The fen has no
  instrument of power and is always the collateral, never the party.
  (world.md)
- Salt-factors buy bond-setters' indentures — twenty years of hands at the
  buyer's speed — and this is the largest single source of factor wealth.
  (world.md)
- Kethren has exported setters under the 1104 Concession for a hundred and
  fifteen years. (world.md)
- The Sur Ellun file has been closed since 1148 and is reopened, quietly and
  fruitlessly, in ch 24. (ch 24, ch 40)

## Courtship & Cultural

- A witnessed marriage on the Shelf is a **merger of accounts**. The entry in
  the Long Book *is* the marriage; the ceremony is a reading of the entry
  aloud. (world.md)
- Marriage transfers future capacity. A drawer who marries pledges her future
  carries into the joint estate, where her spouse's house may pledge them
  forward. (world.md, HARD RULE)
- **Composition (Third Order, 1063):** where an assessment cannot be paid
  within the debtor's working life, a creditor may take it onto their own
  books in exchange for a witnessed merger. Dependents are held harmless
  while the composition stands. (world.md)
- **Compositions may be deferred, and may be accelerated:** on a material
  change in the value of the pledged security, the creditor may demand
  execution within thirty days. (world.md, ch 3, ch 32)
- **Any party may refuse at the reading.** The refusal is recorded, the
  composition voids, and the pledged security is distrained the same day.
  (world.md, HARD RULE — this is the world's answer to who may refuse and at
  what cost)
- Breaking a composition is treated as a foreclosure rather than a scandal,
  because the people ruined are the security and not the parties. (world.md)
- **There is no bond, mate-tie, soul-tether, or prophecy in this world.** No
  character may be given knowledge of another's feelings by any means.
  (world.md, HARD RULE)
- You can read a person's trade off their body at ten paces: whitened
  hairline (cistern drawer), sweet wrists (granary hand), gloved hands
  (setter hiding his grey). The rich are the people who have never carried
  anything. (world.md)
- Full-grey setters are pensioned by ordinance at a third rate and die early
  of injuries they never felt. (world.md, characters.md)
- People the Draw cannot help — broken bones, lost senses, deafness — are
  outside the economy entirely, and the handwork trades (washers, limers,
  spoilers' men) are their recourse and their poverty. (world.md)

## The Ottun Composition — the instrument, in full

- Contracted 1211 between House Nesuir (creditor) and Sahra Ottun (debtor),
  against the assessment of 1201. (world.md)
- **Principal: 2,140 carries.** Outstanding at ch 3: **1,806**. Paid in eight
  years: 334. Clear at her achieved rate: age sixty-two. (world.md, ch 3)
- **Security pledged:** (a) the Sarrow common ground — six villages, ~1,900
  people, tenure through the Nesuir estate; (b) the drawing line of Ottun —
  presently Sahra, thereafter Yeshin, to be assessed at sixteen. (world.md)
- **Alienation of the line.** The security at (b) is a line and runs by
  descent. Issue of the debtor is pledged from birth and displaces the
  collateral heir — a child of Sahra's takes Yeshin's place in the schedule
  the day it is entered. Issue entered outside the merged estate is capacity
  the creditor has pledged forward and cannot produce, and voids the
  composition **for cause**, on the same clause and at the same speed as an
  unrecorded carry. It is a security clause, not a morals clause: the Book
  does not record whose household she keeps. Neither Halim nor Dovra can
  waive it, because the pledge runs past Nesuir to the House. Named aloud by
  Halim in ch 17. (world.md, ch 17, **HARD RULE**)
- **On voiding:** the 1201 entry revives at 2,140 with eight years' accrued
  charge; the fen tenure is distrained; Yeshin is assessed against a live
  entry and set to the pump — twenty years' bonded drawing in the Amrith
  cistern works, which founders drawers by thirty. (world.md)
- **Release requires** full payment, or assumption by a house of standing. A
  bond-setter's indenture — the only instrument open to a man with no estate
  — raises about **280 carries**. (world.md, ch 28)
- **Witnessing dates:** set autumn 1220 (1211); moved to spring 1220 (ch 3);
  moved to high summer 1219 (ch 25); accelerated to the new moon of
  Deepwinter 1219 (ch 32).
- **Discharged 24 Deepwinter 1219** by a credit of **2,306 carries** entered
  by Chief Reckoner Bel Osse in the field ledger on the flats, against 2,140
  outstanding with charge. (ch 44)

## Established In-Story

- Sahra told Yannu about the four hours at twenty-two in ch 18. He knows and
  cannot unknow it. (ch 18)
- Sahra told Yannu she was relieved to sign the composition, in ch 23. It
  cannot be unsaid. (ch 23)
- Yannu told Sahra he keeps a fraction of every load, in ch 23. This is the
  fact the Break Into Three is made of. (ch 23)
- Bel Osse sealed the Whiting survey in ch 24. It is a crime for either of
  them to speak it until ch 38. (ch 24)
- Yannu signed the warrant reopening the north lobe in ch 26, under duress,
  knowing the ground was finished. People set down into it. (ch 26)
- Yannu told Turi about Veth in ch 34. Turi died six chapters later. He tells
  Sahra in ch 45. (ch 34, ch 45)
- The demonstration at the Nine Marks in ch 39 is entered in the House's
  field ledger with Bel Osse's initials. It cannot be un-witnessed. (ch 39)
- The Wallow's live edge is emptied on 24 Deepwinter 1219 and the reach comes
  up clean. It does not weep again. (ch 44)
- The Ottun entry is struck. Yeshin is assessed at sixteen against a clean
  line. (ch 44, ch 45)
- Sarrow-under-Wall is condemned and is not resettled. (ch 31, ch 46)
- Bel Osse begins drafting compulsory setter-service before the tide is in on
  26 Deepwinter, and says so to their faces. It is unresolved at the end of
  the book. (ch 45)
